{
  "analyses": [
    {
      "paper_id": "doi-10-18653-v1-2025-findings-naacl-295",
      "title": "Where is this coming from? Making groundedness count in the evaluation of Document VQA models",
      "research_question": "Can Document VQA evaluation better reflect semantic correctness, spatial grounding, calibration, and robustness by scoring where an answer comes from in the document rather than relying mainly on surface-string similarity?",
      "methodology": "The paper proposes SMuDGE, a configurable composite evaluation metric combining multimodal groundedness with type-aware answer similarity. Groundedness is estimated from the spatial relationship between answer evidence in OCR-derived document regions, while textual, numeric, and hybrid answers receive different surface-matching treatments; an alpha parameter controls the trade-off between grounding and answer similarity. The authors re-score outputs on DocVQA, MP-DocVQA, InfographicVQA, and DUDE, then analyze leaderboard changes, calibration through Expected Calibration Error, ranking robustness, and pairwise human preferences.",
      "key_findings": [
        {
          "finding": "Adding groundedness and answer-type awareness changes Document VQA leaderboard orderings, with numeric and hybrid answers causing larger ranking changes than purely textual answers.",
          "evidence_type": "supported",
          "section": "5.1 Leaderboard analysis"
        },
        {
          "finding": "When SMuDGE gives relatively greater weight to groundedness, higher evaluation scores are associated with lower Expected Calibration Error; the paper selects approximately alpha=0.25 as a useful operating point from the DUDE calibration analysis.",
          "evidence_type": "supported",
          "section": "5.3 Association with calibration"
        },
        {
          "finding": "SMuDGE scores show a stronger relationship between score stability and ranking stability than ANLS, with reported regression coefficients of 0.58 for SMuDGE and 0.33 for ANLS.",
          "evidence_type": "supported",
          "section": "5.4 Association with robustness"
        },
        {
          "finding": "In the human preference experiment, annotators preferred SMuDGE's pairwise ordering in the majority of disagreement cases across DocVQA, MP-DocVQA, and InfographicVQA.",
          "evidence_type": "supported",
          "section": "5.5 Human evaluation"
        },
        {
          "finding": "The human study achieved mean Cohen's kappa of 0.82, indicating high annotator agreement before majority-agreement filtering.",
          "evidence_type": "supported",
          "section": "5.5 Human evaluation"
        },
        {
          "finding": "The proposed score is intentionally parameterized so downstream users can alter the relative importance of grounding and surface similarity.",
          "evidence_type": "supported",
          "section": "3 Proposed methodology"
        }
      ],
      "limitations": [
        "The experiments are restricted to single-span extractive answers.",
        "Handling multi-span answers would require a grounding matcher capable of dealing with an arbitrary number of answer partitions unless the benchmark supplies span-level annotations.",
        "Grounding abstractive answers is outside the scope of the study.",
        "The semantic-type treatment is limited mainly to textual, numeric, and hybrid answers and does not explicitly model categories such as currencies, dates, or timestamps.",
        "Alpha is tuned using DUDE, while the remaining major analyses rely on three related benchmarks, creating a potential benchmark-family bias.",
        "The primary grounding procedure depends on OCR reading order, which can be noisy or misleading; the more general beta-skeleton alternative is slower."
      ],
      "reproducibility": {
        "code_available": false,
        "dataset_available": true,
        "metrics_reported": true
      },
      "confidence_scores": {
        "leaderboard_changes": 0.99,
        "calibration_association": 0.98,
        "robustness_association": 0.98,
        "human_alignment": 0.99,
        "configurable_grounding_weight": 0.99
      },
      "raw_claims": [
        "SMuDGE combines spatial groundedness with answer-type-aware surface similarity.",
        "The evaluation framework exposes a tunable parameter controlling the weighting of groundedness versus answer similarity.",
        "The authors re-evaluate models on four Document VQA benchmarks.",
        "Numeric and hybrid answers produce larger leaderboard changes than textual answers.",
        "Greater emphasis on groundedness is associated with lower model calibration error in the DUDE analysis.",
        "SMuDGE has a stronger reported relationship between score volatility and rank volatility than ANLS.",
        "Three researchers performed the human pairwise preference study.",
        "Mean Cohen's kappa in the human annotations is reported as 0.82.",
        "Human annotators agree with SMuDGE in the majority of evaluated ANLS-versus-SMuDGE disagreement cases.",
        "The grounding experiments exclude abstractive and general multi-span answers."
      ],
      "source_url": "https://arxiv.org/html/2503.19120",
      "access": "full_text"
    },
    {
      "paper_id": "manual-7fdf40b3c6",
      "title": "TRH2TQA: Table Recognition with Hierarchical Relationships to Table Question-Answering on Business Table Images",
      "research_question": "Can explicit recovery of hierarchical relationships in visually complex business tables improve question answering over table images?",
      "methodology": "TRH2TQA is a three-stage pipeline operating on business table images and natural-language questions. A table-recognition module first converts the image into structured HTML containing table structure and recognized text; a post-structure stage then derives headers and hierarchical relationships using predicted column spans and bounding boxes. The recovered table representation and hierarchy are supplied with the question to a table question-answering decoder, and the system is evaluated on the VQAonBD 2023 benchmark.",
      "key_findings": [
        {
          "finding": "The proposed architecture explicitly separates visual table recognition, hierarchical relationship recovery, and table question answering.",
          "evidence_type": "supported",
          "section": "Abstract"
        },
        {
          "finding": "Hierarchical relations are inferred after table recognition using information including predicted column spans and bounding boxes.",
          "evidence_type": "supported",
          "section": "Abstract"
        },
        {
          "finding": "The intermediate representation is HTML containing recognized table structure and textual content rather than an unstructured visual embedding alone.",
          "evidence_type": "supported",
          "section": "Abstract"
        },
        {
          "finding": "The authors report that TRH2TQA improves question-answering performance on the VQAonBD 2023 business-document benchmark.",
          "evidence_type": "supported",
          "section": "Abstract"
        },
        {
          "finding": "The method is specifically motivated by hierarchical tables whose merged cells and indentation make ordinary flat table recognition insufficient.",
          "evidence_type": "supported",
          "section": "Abstract"
        }
      ],
      "limitations": [
        "The accessible HTML source contains the abstract rather than the complete paper, so detailed architectural and ablation claims could not be independently extracted from full text.",
        "The accessible source describes the method specifically for business table images.",
        "The accessible source names VQAonBD 2023 as the evaluation benchmark and does not establish generalization to other table-image domains.",
        "The abstract does not provide sufficient evidence to characterize performance on non-hierarchical documents, spreadsheets with workbook-level semantics, or cross-document provenance tasks."
      ],
      "reproducibility": {
        "code_available": false,
        "dataset_available": true,
        "metrics_reported": true
      },
      "confidence_scores": {
        "three_stage_pipeline": 0.99,
        "hierarchy_from_colspan_bbox": 0.99,
        "html_intermediate_representation": 0.98,
        "vq aonbd_improvement": 0.94,
        "hierarchical_table_focus": 0.99
      },
      "raw_claims": [
        "TRH2TQA targets question answering on business table images.",
        "Its table-recognition stage converts a table image into HTML structure and text.",
        "A post-processing stage identifies headers and hierarchical relationships.",
        "Predicted column spans and bounding boxes are used during hierarchical relationship extraction.",
        "The recovered table information is combined with a natural-language question before answer generation.",
        "The paper reports improved question-answering performance on VQAonBD 2023.",
        "Merged cells and indentation are identified as important difficulties in hierarchical tables."
      ],
      "source_url": "https://openaccess.thecvf.com/content/WACV2025/html/Jirachanchaisiri_TRH2TQA_Table_Recognition_with_Hierarchical_Relationships_to_Table_Question-Answering_on_WACV_2025_paper.html",
      "access": "abstract_only"
    },
    {
      "paper_id": "2511.12003",
      "title": "Look as You Think: Unifying Reasoning and Visual Evidence Attribution for Verifiable Document RAG via Reinforcement Learning",
      "research_question": "Can a vision-language model be trained to produce accurate document-RAG answers while grounding intermediate reasoning steps and final answers to verifiable page-level visual regions with limited stepwise supervision?",
      "methodology": "The paper introduces Chain-of-Evidence, in which textual reasoning steps are paired with page indices and bounding boxes for their supporting evidence, followed by a final answer with its own supporting region. LAT uses two training stages: a cold-start stage creates CoE traces with Gemini 2.5 Pro from 1,000 sampled instances per training dataset, filters them for answer quality, manually corrects bounding-box drift, and performs LoRA supervised fine-tuning; a second stage applies GRPO reinforcement learning. The RL objective combines answer-accuracy, stepwise attribution, final grounding, and format rewards, including semantic comparison between reasoning steps and cropped evidence regions using ColQwen2. Experiments use Qwen2.5-VL-7B-Instruct on Paper-VISA and Wiki-VISA under single-image, multi-image, in-domain, and cross-domain settings.",
      "key_findings": [
        {
          "finding": "Across the reported single- and multi-image evaluations, LAT improves the vanilla model by an average of 8.23% in soft exact match and 47.0% in IoU@0.5.",
          "evidence_type": "supported",
          "section": "Abstract; 5.1 Main Results"
        },
        {
          "finding": "In the in-domain comparison, LAT reports gains of 7.95% in answer exact match and 44.6% in IoU@0.5 over the vanilla model.",
          "evidence_type": "supported",
          "section": "5.1 Attribution-aware performance under in-domain and cross-domain settings"
        },
        {
          "finding": "LAT substantially improves stepwise Chain-of-Evidence attribution quality, with a reported 37.5% gain in stepwise attribution compared with only a 4.0% gain from adding an in-context CoE demonstration.",
          "evidence_type": "supported",
          "section": "5.1 Main Results"
        },
        {
          "finding": "For unanswerable multi-image cases, LAT reports average precision of 65% when producing a no-answer response.",
          "evidence_type": "supported",
          "section": "5.1 Main Results"
        },
        {
          "finding": "LAT outperforms the direct supervised answer-plus-attribution baseline and shows stronger cross-domain generalization in the reported experiments.",
          "evidence_type": "supported",
          "section": "Abstract; 5 Results and Analysis"
        },
        {
          "finding": "The Chain-of-Evidence representation records evidence at reasoning-step granularity as a page index plus a bounding box and separately grounds the final answer.",
          "evidence_type": "supported",
          "section": "3.1 CoE Formalization and Notations"
        }
      ],
      "limitations": [
        "Thresholds used by the stepwise attribution rewards are manually selected from annotated examples rather than learned adaptively.",
        "Training is currently limited to VISA data, whose evidence annotations are predominantly single-hop.",
        "Generalization to multi-hop and cross-source evidence reasoning has not been fully evaluated or supervised.",
        "The cold-start procedure depends on a proprietary Gemini 2.5 Pro model and subsequent manual bounding-box correction, which makes exact independent reproduction of the data-generation stage more involved."
      ],
      "reproducibility": {
        "code_available": true,
        "dataset_available": true,
        "metrics_reported": true
      },
      "confidence_scores": {
        "average_em_iou_gains": 0.99,
        "in_domain_improvement": 0.99,
        "stepwise_attribution_gain": 0.97,
        "no_answer_precision": 0.97,
        "cross_domain_generalization": 0.96,
        "step_level_bbox_provenance": 0.99
      },
      "raw_claims": [
        "Chain-of-Evidence associates reasoning steps with document page indices and visual bounding boxes.",
        "The final answer is also paired with a page and supporting evidence box.",
        "The cold-start stage samples 1,000 instances from each training dataset for CoE generation.",
        "Gemini 2.5 Pro generates initial stepwise reasoning and evidence annotations.",
        "The authors manually verify and correct bounding-box drift before cold-start supervised training.",
        "The reinforcement-learning stage uses GRPO.",
        "LAT optimizes answer accuracy, stepwise evidence attribution, final grounding, and output-format objectives.",
        "Stepwise evidence consistency is measured using representations of the reasoning text and the cropped document region.",
        "Experiments cover both single-image and multi-image document inputs.",
        "LAT reports average improvements of 8.23% in soft exact match and 47.0% in IoU@0.5 relative to the vanilla model.",
        "The released implementation is linked to the PolarisLiu1/LAT GitHub repository.",
        "The authors identify multi-hop and cross-source evidence reasoning as an unresolved direction."
      ],
      "source_url": "https://arxiv.org/html/2511.12003",
      "access": "full_text"
    },
    {
      "paper_id": "2401.00908",
      "title": "DocLLM: A layout-aware generative language model for multimodal document understanding",
      "research_question": "Can a causal language model gain strong visually rich document understanding by incorporating OCR-derived spatial layout directly into attention, without relying on a heavyweight image encoder?",
      "methodology": "DocLLM extends autoregressive language models such as Falcon-1B and Llama2-7B by representing text tokens together with their bounding boxes and introducing disentangled attention over textual and spatial relationships. Pre-training uses autoregressive block infilling over semantically cohesive document text regions instead of relying solely on ordinary next-token prediction. The models are subsequently instruction-tuned on 16 datasets spanning visual question answering, natural-language inference, key-information extraction, and document classification, including both single-page and multi-page documents. Evaluation includes same-dataset/different-split and same-task/different-dataset settings plus ablations of spatial attention, infilling, and decoder masking.",
      "key_findings": [
        {
          "finding": "DocLLM-7B outperforms the compared state-of-the-art LLM baselines on 14 of the 16 datasets in the same-dataset evaluation setting.",
          "evidence_type": "supported",
          "section": "4.3 Downstream Evaluation; 6 Discussion and Findings"
        },
        {
          "finding": "The model generalizes successfully on four of five previously unseen dataset settings, with reported improvements of roughly 15% to 61% for the Llama2-7B-based model on four of those five datasets.",
          "evidence_type": "supported",
          "section": "1 Introduction; 4.3 Downstream Evaluation"
        },
        {
          "finding": "Ablation results show that text-only self-attention has the lowest pre-training next-token-prediction accuracy, while adding spatial interactions improves it; the best reported spatial-attention configuration reaches 39.12 versus 35.43 for text-only attention.",
          "evidence_type": "supported",
          "section": "5 Ablation Studies"
        },
        {
          "finding": "Block infilling with spatial information reaches 39.1 next-token-prediction accuracy in the ablation, compared with 36.2 for causal learning with spatial information and 32.6 for plain causal learning.",
          "evidence_type": "supported",
          "section": "5 Ablation Studies"
        },
        {
          "finding": "A causal decoder performs comparably to, and slightly better than, the tested prefix decoder configurations, so the authors retain the causal architecture.",
          "evidence_type": "supported",
          "section": "5 Ablation Studies"
        },
        {
          "finding": "DocLLM obtains document-layout information from token bounding boxes and deliberately avoids a conventional vision encoder, reducing architectural complexity while retaining spatial structure.",
          "evidence_type": "supported",
          "section": "1 Introduction; 3 DocLLM Framework"
        }
      ],
      "limitations": [
        "DocLLM does not directly encode document pixels or visual appearance; the authors identify lightweight visual integration as future work.",
        "The model depends on OCR-derived text and bounding boxes, while the effect of alternative OCR engines and layout parsers is left for future investigation.",
        "The instruction-tuning data is constructed from templated existing datasets rather than crowdsourced natural instructions and preferences.",
        "The ablation experiments are resource-constrained to a sampled subset of 100,000 pre-training chunks and evaluation on 1,000 unseen documents.",
        "The paper's official public repository contains the paper description and results but does not expose the full training implementation required to reproduce the reported models.",
        "Not all data used to create the complete instruction-tuning mixture is released as a single reproducible dataset."
      ],
      "reproducibility": {
        "code_available": false,
        "dataset_available": false,
        "metrics_reported": true
      },
      "confidence_scores": {
        "fourteen_of_sixteen": 0.99,
        "unseen_dataset_generalization": 0.99,
        "spatial_attention_ablation": 0.99,
        "block_infilling_ablation": 0.99,
        "causal_vs_prefix_decoder": 0.97,
        "no_vision_encoder": 0.99
      },
      "raw_claims": [
        "DocLLM models document text together with token bounding boxes.",
        "It extends causal language-model attention with disentangled spatial attention.",
        "The architecture does not require a conventional image encoder.",
        "Pre-training uses an autoregressive block-infilling objective over document text.",
        "Instruction tuning spans VQA, NLI, key-information extraction, and document classification.",
        "The instruction-tuning mixture contains 16 datasets.",
        "The reported instruction-tuning data contains 635,883 training instances and 96,919 testing instances.",
        "DocLLM-7B is based on Llama2-7B and DocLLM-1B is based on Falcon-1B.",
        "DocLLM is evaluated on both familiar dataset splits and held-out datasets with the same task types.",
        "DocLLM-7B outperforms the compared LLM baselines on 14 of 16 datasets in the main same-dataset setting.",
        "Spatial information improves the pre-training ablation over text-only attention.",
        "Block infilling with spatial information achieves the best reported objective-level ablation result.",
        "The authors leave comparisons across OCR engines and layout parsers to future work.",
        "The authors propose adding visual information to DocLLM in a lightweight manner in future work."
      ],
      "source_url": "https://arxiv.org/html/2401.00908",
      "access": "full_text"
    }
  ],
  "skipped": []
}
